title: How many are wrong?
fullTitle: Your Directory Has 10,000 Listings. How Many Are Wrong?

captions.text: 10,000 listings. The only number the directory has.
A count says how many rows exist, not how many are right.
Problems overlap: one row can carry several flags.
Synthetic, seeded dataset: we know exactly what was planted.
Five checks on the public rows only. Website checks hit a local mock, not real sites.
Last verified is kept apart from last changed and last checked.
Adding the columns together invents problems that do not exist.
The website timed out. In the ground truth, the business is open.
1,038 failed website checks landed on open businesses.
Uncertain cases go to a review queue, not the bin.
Each card carries every reason it was flagged.
A decision records evidence, timestamp and reviewer.
Last checked moves. Last verified does not.
The checker also missed planted problems. They are reported as missed.
A failed website check is a lead to investigate, not proof.
